models.note: Usage by model. Models were used over different periods and for different work, so differences also carry timing and task differences.

tip.turns: A turn is one model call. Units differ by tool, so compare within one tool.
tip.mistakes: Edit mismatches, missing files and edits before reading: the errors closest to model slips. Command failures and permission blocks are not included.
tip.response: From the request to the last answer. Includes approval waits and long-running commands.
tip.context: Tokens the model reads each turn (new input + cache).

models.mistakesNA: Not distinguished in this tool's logs
models.none: No model usage in the session logs yet.

interruptTip.claude: Claude Code: the user pressed stop

detail.tokensNote: Cache read is the same conversation read again on every turn, counted apart from new input.
detail.cost: Cost recorded in the log (OpenCode value)
detail.limitsNote: Account-wide, the same for every Codex model. Plan: {{plan}}
detail.distTooFew: Fewer than {{min}} requests ({{n}}), so no distribution is shown.
detail.maxSession: Open the session with the maximum: {{title}}
detail.legend: Whiskers min–max · box p25–p75 · line median · dot mean · tick p90

kindDesc.mistake: Edit mismatch, missing file, edit before reading
kindDesc.command: Non-zero exit: tests, builds (often part of normal work)
kindDesc.policy: Blocked by permission rules or hooks

detail.errorsCodex: Codex logs record command failures only.
detail.errorsOpencode: OpenCode logs don't record the kind of error.

models.metricsUnavailable: These logs do not collect all metrics. Unavailable values are shown as —, not zero.

leaderboard.noPoints: No combinations with at least 30 requests and a known price
leaderboard.priceError: Enter valid non-negative prices. The price could not be saved.
leaderboard.costNote: API prices as of {{date}}; five-minute cache writes. Context tiers in the price table are applied. Subscription bills, fast-mode premiums, cache storage and external tools are not included. The chart and table use the median cost of measured model turns, including subagents and unfinished requests. The median cost per completed request is shown in detail.
leaderboard.dragZoom: Drag an empty chart area to zoom into a region. Reset restores the full range.

efficiency.mixedTools: Tool differences are mixed into this comparison.
efficiency.priceNote: Price date: {{date}} · {{source}}. API price equivalent, not subscription spending. The representative cost is the median per measured model turn, including subagents and unfinished requests. Request medians and the distribution use completed requests.
efficiency.reindexCosts: Cost detail will appear after the session index updates.

hooks.deleteBody: Moves {{name}} and its scripts to .trash. Its entries leave the tools on the next sync.

timingHint.before-tool: Right before a command or edit runs. Some tools can stop it here.
timingHint.after-tool: Right after a tool finishes. For formatting, linting and logging.
timingHint.prompt: When you send a prompt. Add context or check it.
timingHint.stop: When the agent finishes a reply. For notifications.
timingHint.session-start: When a session opens. Check the environment or log it.
timingHint.notification: When the tool waits for your permission or input.

hooks.triggersHint: Each tool has its own event names and options. The same option is not guaranteed to behave the same in every tool.
hooks.matcherAll: Leave empty for every tool call
hooks.matcherHint: A pattern of tool names. Tool names differ per tool.
hooks.timeoutMs: Written to Gemini CLI in milliseconds

toolInput.copilot: JSON on stdin: toolName, toolArgs (a JSON string)

toolBlock.claude: exit 2 (stderr is the reason) or JSON hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision
toolBlock.copilot: Any non-zero exit or JSON permissionDecision: deny (errors also stop the tool)
toolBlock.qwen: exit 2 (stderr is the reason) or JSON hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision

hooks.codexTrust: Codex runs a new or changed hook only after you trust it in /hooks.
hooks.grokViaClaude: Grok runs this hook from Claude Code's settings
hooks.ownCreated: Created a {{tool}}-only script from the shared one
hooks.editedHint: Syncing restores the library version (the edited copy is backed up).

notify.title: Notify me
notify.desc: When a reply ends or the agent waits for you: on this Mac or on your phone (ntfy, Slack)

guard.title: Block dangerous commands
guard.desc: Stop shell commands like rm -rf / or git push --force before they run

format.title: Format edited files
format.desc: Run a formatter on the changed files once a reply ends (or after each edit)

log.title: Keep a log
log.desc: Append the time, tool and folder to a log file

ask.title: Check with a plain-language rule
ask.desc: Write a rule in plain words; an AI checks each event against it and lets it through or stops it

script.title: Run a command or script
script.desc: Run a command or shell script with the tool's raw input

verify.title: Check before finishing
verify.desc: Run the project's tests when the agent says it's done, and send it back if they fail

protect.title: Protect files
protect.desc: Stop edits to .env, keys, lock files and .git

context.title: Brief the agent at session start
context.desc: Tell it the current branch, uncommitted changes and your notes

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint each reply
checkpoint.desc: Save the work tree when a reply ends, so you can go back to any point

opt.title: Title
opt.patternsHint: One per line. A command that contains any of these is stopped.
opt.commandHint: Runs with the edited file's path added at the end.

urlEnvHint.ntfy: Put your ntfy topic URL (https://ntfy.sh/…) in this variable, e.g. through Bitwarden. Illithid never stores the address.
urlEnvHint.slack: Put your Slack incoming webhook URL in this variable, e.g. through Bitwarden. Illithid never stores the address.

opt.project: Add the project folder name to the title
opt.testCommandHint: Leave empty to pick it from the project: npm test, pytest, go test, cargo test.
opt.protectPatternsHint: One file pattern per line (* and ? work). Patterns with / match the path.
opt.git: Include the git branch and uncommitted changes
opt.commandHintStop: Runs once at the end of a reply, with every changed file at the end.

modeHint.snapshot: Saved under refs/illithid/checkpoints without touching your files, index or branch; the latest 50 are kept. Go back with: git restore --source <checkpoint> -- .
modeHint.commit: Commits everything changed on the current branch (git add -A). Check your .gitignore so secrets are not committed.

opt.judgeHint: Claude Code checks with its built-in prompt hook. Other tools run this CLI once more to check (slower, uses your plan).
opt.modelHint: Leave empty for the CLI's default.
opt.judgeSlow: Before an action, every command waits for the check. Prefer “When a reply finishes” unless you need it.
opt.judgeFailOpen: For tools that run a judging CLI, a missing CLI, a failed command or an invalid JSON verdict skips the check and lets the event continue. Skipped checks are reported on stderr. Claude Code uses its own prompt-hook behavior.

hooks.instructionHint: An AI reads this rule with the event and lets it through or stops it.
hooks.instructionExample: If the tests have not passed yet, keep working.
hooks.scriptStarter: Starts with a template script. Edit it after creating.
hooks.nameTaken: A hook with this name exists
hooks.windowsTitle: Hooks are not available on Windows yet
hooks.windowsBody: You can keep and edit hooks in the library, but Illithid does not write them to any tool on Windows yet. They reach your tools on macOS.

unsupported.noEvent: No event for this timing in {{tool}}
unsupported.noFilePath: Not in {{tool}}: its hooks aren't told which file was edited
unsupported.claudeOnly: Not in {{tool}}: no judgment hooks (Claude Code only)
unsupported.noContext: Not in {{tool}}: it ignores what a session start hook says

hooks.pendingHint: Sync to write this hook into the tools.
hooks.noTools: No tool in use can run this hook.
hooks.generated: Generated by Illithid from the options. Read-only.
hooks.promptGenerated: The prompt Illithid writes to Claude Code
hooks.convertBody: The {{tool}} script becomes this hook's run.sh and every tool runs it. The options no longer apply.
hooks.libScriptHint: Runs a script from Scripts. Edit it there; every hook using it follows.
hooks.contextNoteHint: Added to the session start, e.g. house rules or where to look first.
hooks.contextNoteExample: Run npm test before you finish. Never edit generated files.
hooks.timeoutAllHint: Seconds, the same for every tool. Empty = each tool's default.

permissions.deleteBody: Removes the rule for {{command}}. The tools drop it on the next sync.
permissions.emptyHint: Add a rule to block, ask about or allow a shell command in every tool.

decisionHint.ask: The agent asks you before running these.
decisionHint.allow: The agent runs these without asking.

permissions.matchPrefixHint: Also covers longer commands (git push --force origin main).
permissions.commandHint: The words a command starts with. Quotes group words, like in a shell.
permissions.duplicate: This command already has a rule
permissions.guardsHint: These hooks check commands too, matching any part of the command. Edit them in Hooks.
permissions.claudeOnly: {{count}} Claude Code-only rules in permissions.json are kept as they are.
permissions.restartHint: Codex and Grok CLI read the rules when a session starts. Copilot keeps no block rules, so Illithid blocks them with a check hook.
permissions.copilotHook: Blocked by an Illithid check hook (Copilot keeps no block rules)
permissions.copilotNo: Copilot can't keep ask or allow rules
permissions.grokViaClaude: Grok CLI reads these from Claude Code's settings
permissions.codexPrefix: Codex matches the start of the command, so this also covers longer commands
permissions.groupDeleteBody: Removes the group {{name}} and its {{count}} rules. The tools drop them on the next sync.
permissions.groupNameHint: Optional. Left empty, the commands go in no group and the description goes on each rule.
permissions.groupNameTaken: A group with this name exists
permissions.groupCommandsHint: One command per line. Change what to do for each line below.
permissions.mcpToolsHint: Set in each server's permissions tab. Open one to change it.

scripts.deleteUsed: Moves {{name}} to .trash. The {{count}} hooks using it each keep a copy as their own script.
scripts.nameTaken: A script with this name exists
scripts.kindFileHint: One .sh file. Good for short scripts.
scripts.kindFolderHint: A folder with run.sh and any other files it calls by relative path. The tools get the whole folder.
scripts.toFolderHint: To keep other files next to it
scripts.toFolderBody: {{name}}.sh becomes {{name}}/run.sh so other files can sit next to it. Hooks using this script keep it.
scripts.importEntryHint: Path in the folder. Left empty: its SCRIPT.md's, else run.sh
scripts.importHint: The folder is copied into the library; the original stays where it is.
scripts.deleteFolderUsed: {{count}} hooks use {{name}}, so it can't be deleted. Point them at another script first.
scripts.problemTitle: The tools don't get this script

problem.ignoredFolder: It holds .git, node_modules, .venv or __pycache__. Keep those out of the folder.
problem.noEntry: The file it runs is missing.

scripts.fileExists: A file with this path exists
